items.question: What temporal and cosmic conditions are absent from the realized state?
premises: The realized state is not past.
The realized state is not future.
The realized state is devoid of continuance and dissolution.
items.inference: The realized state transcends temporal categories and cosmic phases of persistence and dissolution.
items.plain_english: It is not past, not future, and devoid of continuance and dissolution.

items.question: What personal identities and relations of bondage are denied in realization?
premises: There is no separate someone as I.
There is no separate someone as mine.
There is neither a bound one nor an obstructor.
items.inference: Realization negates egoic identity, possessive relation, and the duality of bound and binder.
items.plain_english: I am no one, no one is mine; there is none bound and no obstructor.

items.question: In which ordinary activities does the yogin remain established without disruption?
premises: The yogin may be going or standing.
The yogin may be sleeping or waking.
The yogin may be eating or even in sexual union.
items.inference: The yogin's state persists unchanged across all ordinary bodily activities.
items.plain_english: Whether going, standing, sleeping, waking, eating, or even in sexual union.

rows.grounds: with objects of the senses; compound indriya+artha

items.question: What corrective engagement with sense objects should the yogin never undertake?
premises: Sense objects are the potential field of engagement.
Remedy or corrective effort is a possible response.
Such remedy should never be made through sense objects.
items.inference: The yogin should not seek adjustment or cure by engaging with sense objects.
items.plain_english: One should never make any remedy through sense objects.

items.question: How does the liberated yogin move through the world in this state?
premises: The yogin moves in the manner described.
The comparison is to fire in a forest.
Forest fire moves freely and consumes without restraint.
items.inference: The yogin moves freely and unimpeded, like fire in a forest.
items.plain_english: Thus the yogin moves like fire in a forest.

items.question: Which yogic supports are absent in the described transcendent condition?
premises: The state is devoid of the lunar principle.
The state is likewise devoid of the fiery principle.
The state is free from breath-control.
items.inference: The transcendent condition does not depend on lunar, solar, or breath-control practices.
uncertainties: The exact referents of soma and vahni in this context may be physiological or symbolic.
items.plain_english: It is devoid of moon and fire, and free from breath-control.

items.question: What long-standing devotion to the guru characterizes the qualified recipient?
premises: The guru has been worshipped by someone.
This worship extends over thousands of births.
The worship is performed with devotion.
items.inference: The qualified recipient is one who has devotedly worshipped the guru across countless lifetimes.
items.plain_english: By whom the guru has been worshipped with devotion for thousands of births.

items.question: What unwavering devotion within the yogini circle marks the qualified practitioner?
premises: The context is the circle of the yogini Rakini.
The practitioner possesses devotion there.
That devotion is very firm and unwavering.
items.inference: The qualified practitioner has unwavering devotion in the circle of the yogini Rakini.
uncertainties: The specific identity or function of Rākiṇī in this text is not fully specified here.
items.plain_english: Whose devotion is very firm in the circle of the yogini Rakini.

rows.grounds: that which is to be known

items.question: What kind of knowable reality is realized when the body is transcended?
premises: There is a moment of transcending the body.
At that moment something becomes knowable.
That knowable is non-body and devoid of body.
items.inference: Transcending the body reveals a knowable reality that is entirely non-bodily.
items.plain_english: When the knowable that transcends the body is realized, it is non-body and devoid of body.

rows.grounds: made of that, identified with that

items.question: What eternal attainment follows absorption into that non-bodily reality?
premises: One becomes absorbed in that reality.
In that absorption one becomes of that nature.
One finds the self as the eternal state.
items.inference: Absorption into that reality yields realization of the self as the eternal state.
uncertainties: The form śvāśvataṃ appears non-standard; taken as equivalent to śāśvatam.
items.plain_english: Absorbed in that, becoming of that nature, one finds the self as the eternal state.

items.question: What qualities define the state of liberation described here?
premises: Liberation is devoid of latent impressions.
The self is satisfied.
The self is free from disease or affliction.
items.inference: Liberation is characterized by absence of impressions, contentment, and freedom from affliction.
items.plain_english: Liberation is devoid of latent impressions; the self is satisfied and free from affliction.

rows.grounds: for that very person; compound tasya+eva

items.question: What all-pervading manifestation quickly arises for that liberated being?
premises: Something arises for that person.
It arises quickly.
It is all and all-pervading for that very person.
items.inference: For that liberated being, the all-pervading totality manifests swiftly.
uncertainties: The subject of pravartate is elliptic; taken as the all-pervading reality.
items.plain_english: For him it quickly arises; for him alone all becomes all-pervading.

items.question: Why are bodily afflictions and their associated delusions deemed meaningless?
premises: All those are delusions.
They are associated with bodily afflictions.
They are declared meaningless.
items.inference: Delusions tied to bodily afflictions lack ultimate meaning for the realized one.
uncertainties: The syntactic agreement of nirarthakam with plural mohāni is irregular; sense taken as predicative.
items.plain_english: All those delusions, along with bodily afflictions, are meaningless.

items.question: What misplaced satisfaction characterizes those who ponder many textual meanings?
premises: Some people ponder the meanings of many texts.
They are satisfied.
Their satisfaction rests on what is meaningless.
items.inference: Thinkers absorbed in many textual meanings may be satisfied with what is ultimately meaningless.
items.plain_english: And those who ponder the meanings of many texts are satisfied with meaninglessness.

items.question: Why can vast textual learning not produce knowledge in the arrogant?
premises: The arrogant may possess hundreds of crores of texts.
Knowledge is the desired attainment.
Arrogance prevents knowledge from arising.
items.inference: Even immense textual learning cannot yield knowledge for the arrogant.
items.plain_english: How can the arrogant gain knowledge, even with hundreds of crores of texts?

items.question: What direct vision of the all-pervading hero within the body is decisive?
premises: There is an Akula hero dwelling in the body.
That hero is all-pervading.
One may directly see that hero.
items.inference: Direct vision of the all-pervading Akula hero within the body is a decisive realization.
uncertainties: The compound akula vīram may be read as a title or as two qualities; taken as the Akula hero.
items.plain_english: When one sees the all-pervading Akula hero dwelling in the body.

rows.grounds: in the domain of ritual works; compound karma+kāṇḍa

items.question: Which ritual and contemplative observances are negated in this realization?
premises: Ritual action is negated.
Truthfulness or purity in the ritual section is negated.
Contemplation is negated.
items.inference: This realization stands apart from ritual action, ritual purity, and contemplative cultivation.
uncertainties: The pairing satya śaucaṃ is syntactically compressed; taken as purity/truthfulness observances.
items.plain_english: There is no ritual action, no truthfulness or purity in the ritual section, and no contemplation.

items.question: What motivates people to practice conventional observances according to this critique?
premises: Conventional conducts are practiced by people.
Those people are bewildered by delusion.
Their practice arises from that bewilderment.
items.inference: Conventional observances are practiced by people confused by delusion.
items.plain_english: Conventional conducts are practiced by people bewildered by delusion.

rows.grounds: by false or poor scholars; compound ku+paṇḍita

items.question: Who fabricates the artificial bondages that prevail in the world?
premises: Artificial bondages exist in the world.
These bondages are imagined constructs.
They are imagined by bad scholars.
items.inference: False scholars fabricate the artificial bondages that bind people in the world.
items.plain_english: Artificial bondages in the world are imagined by bad scholars.

items.question: Which worldly attainments are listed as objects of pursuit in this critique?
premises: Various supernatural powers exist in the world.
Attainment of the netherworld is pursued.
Alchemy is pursued.
items.inference: Supernatural powers, netherworld attainment, and alchemy are worldly pursuits named here.
items.plain_english: Various supernatural powers in the world, the netherworld, and alchemy.

items.question: What is the spiritual consequence of pursuing the listed worldly attainments?
premises: All those pursuits are bound by a noose.
They lead in a downward direction.
They give a downward path.
items.inference: These worldly attainments bind and lead one along a downward path.
uncertainties: baddhaḥ appears singular in form but agrees in sense with plural sarve te; taken as collective.
items.plain_english: All of them are bound by a noose and lead to a downward path.

items.question: Why is the bliss of realization unlike the pleasure described from liquor?
premises: The bliss of liquor can be described.
Such described bliss does not truly arise in that way.
The comparison negates equivalence.
items.inference: The bliss of realization cannot be equated with or produced like the described pleasure of liquor.
uncertainties: The verse is elliptical; the comparison implies a higher bliss not captured by description.
items.plain_english: Just as the bliss of liquor is described, it does not truly arise in that way.

items.question: What supreme essence beyond essence do deluded people fail to know?
premises: Deluded people do not know.
There is something more essential than essence.
That more essential reality is supreme.
items.inference: Deluded people fail to know the supreme reality that is more essential than essence itself.
items.plain_english: Deluded people do not know the supreme, more essential than essence.

items.question: What condition beyond thought defines the true yogin and contemplator of yoga?
premises: A yogin may go beyond thought.
When beyond thought, he is truly a yogin.
He is then a contemplator of yoga.
items.inference: The true yogin and contemplator of yoga is one who has gone beyond thought.
items.plain_english: When the yogin is beyond thought, he is truly a yogin, a contemplator of yoga.
